behaviour: Unit tests of the diff, of insert and delete shifting, and of style operations on the range model.
rules: Import from ../src/textDiff and ../src/textRanges; hashString from ../src/index. Build elements as plain { originalText, textRanges } objects. T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", where "120ms" is [20, 25). RED = "#e03131", BLUE = "#1971c2", YELLOW = "#ffec99".
Seed a range with applyTextRangeStyle({ originalText: T }, { start: 20, end: 25 }, { color: RED }). Assert offsets through textRanges.ranges and getTextStyleRuns, never on an id value.

Fixtures, text: const PROSE = "Bid request timeout 120ms applies to every exchange in the primary region. When the auction server misses that window the request is dropped and the slot is sold through the fallback path. Review the latency dashboard before changing this value, and tell the on-call engineer about any change that touches the pricing service."; const ADDED = "Before the next release the team agreed to review every setting that controls how long a request may wait, and to write down who owns each one. The list below is the current state of that work, and it will change as the review goes on through the rest of the quarter, so please read it again before you rely on any of these numbers. "; (it ends with a space and is 333 characters; ADDED.slice(0, 100) is the 100-character form). const DIGITS = Array.from({ length: 2500 }, (_, i) => String(i).padStart(4, "0")).join(""); const seeded = (length: number, seed: number) => { let state = seed; let out = ""; for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) { state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff; out += String.fromCharCode(97 + ((state >>> 16) % 26)); } return out; }; const W = seeded(10_000, 12345);

Fixtures, helpers: const repeatTo = (text: string, length: number) => { let out = ""; while (out.length < length) { out += `${text} `; } return out.slice(0, length); }; const proseNote = (lineCount: number) => { const lines: string[] = []; let at = 0; while (lines.length < lineCount) { lines.push(PROSE.slice(at, at + 58).trim()); at = (at + 58) % (PROSE.length - 60); } return lines.join("
"); }; const digitNote = (lineCount: number) => Array.from({ length: lineCount }, (_, i) => DIGITS.slice(i * 60, i * 60 + 58)).join("
"); const indentAll = (text: string) => text.split("
").map((line) => `    ${line}`).join("
"); const spansOf = (text: string): [number, number][] => [...text.matchAll(/[^\s]+/g)].map((match) => [match.index!, match.index! + match[0].length]); const applyHunks = (oldText: string, newText: string, hunks: readonly TextHunk[]) => { let out = ""; let at = 0; for (const hunk of hunks) { out += oldText.slice(at, hunk.oldStart) + newText.slice(hunk.newStart, hunk.newEnd); at = hunk.oldEnd; } return out + oldText.slice(at); };
Every long-edit test asserts true offsets and that the text at those offsets is the same word. Never widen an assertion to pass: if a true offset fails, the code is wrong.

behaviour: Tests of concurrent edits: carrying in both arrival orders, no stale offsets, convergence across clients, removals staying removed, and a remote update dropped while editing. Also the diff budget, the meter's charges, and the final diff pass.
rules: Helpers: T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", W = `Urgent: ${T}`, RED = "#e03131". version(element, text, version, versionNonce) returns { ...element, originalText: text, text, version, versionNonce, index: "a0" }. run(local, remote, appState = {}) returns reconcileElements(cloneJSON([local]), cloneJSON([remote]) as RemoteExcalidrawElement[], appState as AppState)[0]. Text changes on a version go through shiftTextRanges when that version already has ranges.

A range edit is { ...element, textRanges: applyTextRangeStyle(element, span, style), version, versionNonce } built by spreading, so the test sets version and nonce itself. Lower versionNonce wins a tie, as in reconcile today.

sync(local, remote) is the path Collab._reconcileElements takes after restore: existing = cloneJSON([local]); return bumpElementVersions(reconcileElements(existing, cloneJSON([remote]) as RemoteExcalidrawElement[], {} as AppState), existing)[0]. bumpElementVersions comes from ../../data/restore. Never assert a bumped versionNonce's value, which is random: spread a fixed versionNonce over a bumped element where a test needs to know who wins next.

Client convergence is expect(a).toEqual(b) on whole elements, so version, versionNonce, originalText and textRanges must all agree. Between run calls that holds at once. After sync, the two clients of an equal-version race differ in version, versionNonce and updated until the next delivery, so before it assert originalText and textRanges only, and after it assert whole elements.
Assert a carried offset with text.slice(start, end) === "120ms", which is what stale offsets would break.

vi.mock block, exactly: vi.mock("@excalidraw/element/textDiff", async (importOriginal) => { const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import("@excalidraw/element/textDiff")>(); return { ...actual, diffText: vi.fn(actual.diffText) }; }); It wraps diffText over the original, so every other test in the file behaves as before, and it also catches the relative import inside textRangeMerge.ts. The unit of work this test counts is the diffText call and its result. No test here reads a clock.

diff budget fixtures. const seeded = (length: number, seed: number) => { let state = seed; let out = ""; for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) { state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff; out += String.fromCharCode(97 + ((state >>> 16) % 26)); } return out; }; const LONG = seeded(10_000, 12345); (W already names another text in this file.) const element = (text: string, ver: number, versionNonce: number, ranges: ExcalidrawTextRange[]): ExcalidrawTextElement => ({ ...version({ ...newTextElement({ text: T, originalText: T, x: 0, y: 0 }), id: "budget" }, text, ver, versionNonce), textRanges: { textHash: hashString(text), ranges } }); textHash must be hashString of that element's own originalText, or sanitizeTextRanges drops the whole container. const carried = (id: string, z: number, text: string): ExcalidrawTextRange => ({ id, start: 0, end: 5, z, color: RED, origin: { version: 1, versionNonce: z, text, start: 10, end: 20 } }); The record's own start and end are ignored, since the merge maps from origin.

diff budget scenario, shared by the first two tests of that describe. const winner = element(LONG, 9, 1, Array.from({ length: 1024 }, (_, i) => carried(`r${String(i).padStart(4, "0")}`, i + 2, seeded(100, i + 1)))); const l1 = element(T, 5, 2, [carried("zzzz", 5000, LONG.slice(5000, 5100))]); const l2 = element(T, 4, 3, [0, 1, 2].map((i) => carried(`a${i}`, 1, seeded(100, 5000 + i)))); Every version holds ranges, because mergeTextRanges returns early when the other side has none. The union is over MAX_TEXT_RANGES: l2's records have the lowest z, so the cap drops them, and they are the doomed records of Gate 3. mergeTextRanges is called directly, because the arrival order under test is the order of merges, and reconcile would pick the same base in both.
The true offset is [5010, 5020). It is right, and it stays: if the test fails there, the mapping is wrong, so fix the code. Never change that expected value to match an output.

The test "a meter pays for the whole run it reads". Why this input: the exact spent tests above never reach meter.left -= length, because each pair has no common run, or a run the trim's seed already holds, so every candidate returns at the bestLength check. This pair has a run the seed does not hold, and the test reads what a limited meter buys, not a total. Its body, exactly, in this order, in one it: const letters = (from: number, length: number) => String.fromCharCode(...Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => from + i)); const short = letters(0x5600, 500); const long = letters(0x6000, 1000); const a = `${letters(0x4e00, 250)}${short}${letters(0x5000, 250)}${long}q`; const b = `${letters(0x5200, 250)}${short}${letters(0x5400, 250)}${long}z`; const index = 4 * a.length + b.length; const edge = { oldStart: 2000, oldEnd: 2001, newStart: 2000, newEnd: 2001 }; const bothRuns = [{ oldStart: 0, oldEnd: 250, newStart: 0, newEnd: 250 }, { oldStart: 750, oldEnd: 1000, newStart: 750, newEnd: 1000 }, edge]; then expect(diffText(a, b)).toEqual(bothRuns); expect(diffText(a, b, { left: index + 1100 })).toEqual(bothRuns); expect(diffText(a, b, { left: index + 1000 })).toEqual([{ oldStart: 0, oldEnd: 1000, newStart: 0, newEnd: 1000 }, edge]); Before the first expect add the one comment: // long starts where the search first looks, so nothing is read backward. a and b are 2,001 characters each and every letters range is a different block of code points, so the only common runs are short and long. long starts at offset 1000 of both, which is (0 + 2001) >>> 1, and the characters before it differ, so back is 0 and the run's whole price is the forward charge of 1,000. A meter of index + 1000 is emptied by that run, so the search stops before it reaches short; a meter of index + 1100 is not, so it finds both. No test here reads a clock. Never change an expected value to pass: if this fails, the charge is wrong.

behaviour: jsdom tests that apply colour and highlight to an editor selection and assert the element data, the preview layer, and the controls.
rules: Setup: beforeEach await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />), with `const { h } = window;` and unmountComponent() at the top of the file, as textWysiwyg.test.tsx does.

startEditing(text = T): element = API.createElement({ type: "text", text }); API.setElements([element]); API.setSelectedElements([element]); Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER); return getTextEditor(). T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", RED = "#e03131", YELLOW = "#ffec99".

Apply with act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { color: RED })), using actionChangeTextHighlight or actionResetTextStyle in the same way; select with editor.setSelectionRange(start, end) first. Actions come from ../actions.
Find the preview with document.querySelector(`.${PREVIEW_CLASS_NAME}`). jsdom normalizes style colours to rgb, so compare with colorToHex(span.style.color) and colorToHex(span.style.backgroundColor).

Constants and helpers for the long-note tests, at the top of the file: const PROSE = "Bid request timeout 120ms applies to every exchange in the primary region. When the auction server misses that window the request is dropped and the slot is sold through the fallback path. Review the latency dashboard before changing this value, and tell the on-call engineer about any change that touches the pricing service."; const ADDED = "Before the next release the team agreed to review every setting that controls how long a request may wait, and to write down who owns each one. The list below is the current state of that work, and it will change as the review goes on through the rest of the quarter, so please read it again before you rely on any of these numbers. "; (ends with a space; 333 characters; it must not start with T, so that the additions are really new). const DIGITS = Array.from({ length: 2500 }, (_, i) => String(i).padStart(4, "0")).join(""); const repeatTo = (text: string, length: number) => { let out = ""; while (out.length < length) { out += `${text} `; } return out.slice(0, length); }; const proseNote = (lineCount: number) => { const lines: string[] = []; let at = 0; while (lines.length < lineCount) { lines.push(PROSE.slice(at, at + 58).trim()); at = (at + 58) % (PROSE.length - 60); } return lines.join("
"); }; const digitNote = (lineCount: number) => Array.from({ length: lineCount }, (_, i) => DIGITS.slice(i * 60, i * 60 + 58)).join("
"); const indentAll = (text: string) => text.split("
").map((line) => `    ${line}`).join("
"); const colour = (editor: HTMLTextAreaElement, start: number, end: number) => { editor.setSelectionRange(start, end); act(() => { h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { color: RED }); }); };

Multi-line Tab goes through the real editor, never through a direct shiftTextRanges call. Given text with a word at [at, at + length), and lineCount = text.slice(0, at).split("\n").length: editor = await startEditing(text); colour(editor, at, at + length); editor.setSelectionRange(0, editor.value.length); fireEvent.keyDown(editor, { key: KEYS.TAB }), with shiftKey: true added for Shift+Tab. Tab keeps the editor open and the ranges update on its input event, so assert straight after keyDown, on h.elements[0] as ExcalidrawTextElement. The true start after Tab is at + 4 * lineCount. A Shift+Tab test starts from indentAll(text) with its word at at + 4 * lineCount, and the true start after it is at.

Every long-note test asserts getTextStyleRuns(element) toEqual the one true run, element.originalText, and that element.originalText.slice(run.start, run.end) is the same word as before. Never widen an assertion to pass: if a true offset fails, the code is wrong.

uses.reason: Imports and helpers for driving the text editor.

sites.rule: Complete: typed before Gate 4, and this file does not change this round. Its packet is not dispatched.

behaviour: Tests that ranges survive bound-text containers, font changes, list markers, and undo and redo.
rules: Setup: beforeEach await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />). Seed ranges with newElementWith(text, { textRanges: applyTextRangeStyle(text, span, style) }) before API.setElements, never with mutateElement. RED = "#e03131", T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", W = `Urgent: ${T}`.

History: put the starting element in with API.updateScene({ elements: [element], captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }), edit through the text editor as in U30, leave with Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor), then use Keyboard.undo() and Keyboard.redo(). A remote change is API.updateScene({ elements, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER }).

After every history step assert the check noStale(element): for each run of getTextStyleRuns(element), element.originalText.slice(run.start, run.end) is the expected word, and sanitizeTextRanges(element.textRanges, element.originalText) is defined.
